title: Coherent substitution of normalized systems into completed operations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For each such scheme $W$ let $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ on its small pro-etale site and $R_W=\varprojlim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use normalized coherent coefficient systems [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for the coherent reduction system and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, with actual quotient transitions and total derived limit [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Let $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ denote the canonical coherent counit on a normalized system [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W$ be completed derived tensor and $\widehat F_f=Lf^*$ completed pullback for a scheme map $f:X\to Y$, defined by the quotient complexes and derived limit of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For normalized systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, put $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$ and $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$, with their canonical coherent coefficient transitions. These systems are normalized. There are natural identifications
$$\widehat T_W(\mathcal L_WA,\mathcal L_WN)\cong\mathcal L_W T_W(A,N),\qquad
\widehat F_f(\mathcal L_YC)\cong\mathcal L_X F_f(C).$$
They are the images under $\mathcal L$ of $T_W(e_A,e_N)$ and $F_f(e_C)$ after substituting the defining reduction systems for the inputs. In particular they are comparisons in the derived system categories before taking the limit.

For any finite well-typed expression formed from normalized input systems, the coefficient unit systems $(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, $T_W$, and $F_f$, the corresponding expression in completed operations on their limits is naturally identified with the limit of the whole expression in systems. Its coherent reduction is identified with that whole system by the counit, including every quotient transition. Under these identifications, the associator, action unitors and Koszul-signed symmetry of completed tensor are the limits of the corresponding canonical total-complex system maps, and the canonical composition comparison of completed pullbacks is the limit of the finite adjunction-normalized composition maps. These identifications are natural for morphisms of all the input systems and compatible with substitution of one such expression into another.

proof.text: Work in the enhanced section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], not in a category of independently specified evaluated derived objects. It supplies tensor, coefficient extension, inverse image and their comparisons on whole systems. On each ringed site choose flat-term K-flat representatives by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] their total tensor remains such a representative, and by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] so does pullback, including pullback along a coefficient quotient. Consequently the ordinary total-complex formulas compute every finite derived expression used below, even for complexes unbounded in both directions. The simultaneous section models retain the transition maps and coherence of those formulas.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); enhanced section models are the cited agent-formulated input

proof.text:
Fix $m\ge n$ and write $q^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with this ring map. The adjoint transition for $T_W(A,N)$ is the composite
$$q^*(A_m\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}N_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*A_m\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}q^*N_m\xrightarrow{\alpha^A_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^N_{m,n}}A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n.$$
Both arrows are invertible by the cited comparison and [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. This is the adjoint of the actual tensor transition: on flat representatives it sends $(a\otimes x)\otimes b$ to $\tau_A(a)\otimes b\tau_N(x)$. The same formula for $r\ge m\ge n$ uses $q_{r,n}=q_{m,n}q_{r,m}$ and the two input cocycles, so gives the quotient cocycle. The section model of step 1 supplies the coherent system, and hence $T_W(A,N)$ is normalized.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), applied to coefficient extension; normalization is the explicit displayed composite

proof.text:
For pullback, use the coefficient square $B_{Y,m}\to B_{Y,n}$, $B_{X,m}\to B_{X,n}$ over $f^{-1}$. It commutes since all four structure maps come from constant sections. In [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] set $R=B_{Y,m}$, $R'=B_{Y,n}$, $S=B_{X,m}$, $S'=B_{X,n}$. Its scalar-association map $\kappa$ identifies
$$q_X^*Lf_m^*C_m\cong Lf_n^*q_Y^*C_m;$$
the indicated direction is $\kappa^{-1}$, obtained by inserting $1$ in the intermediate scalar factor. The scalar-association formulas and step 1 compute this isomorphism on flat-term K-flat representatives. Compose with $Lf_n^*(\alpha^C_{m,n})$ to get the adjoint transition of $F_f(C)$; both factors are invertible by scalar association and [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. The actual transition is the canonical coefficient-extension unit followed by this adjoint: the input transition factors as $C_m\to\operatorname{Res}q_Y^*C_m\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}\alpha^C_{m,n}}\operatorname{Res}C_n$. Thus no hypothesis that an arbitrary normalized system has canonical scalar-extension transitions is needed. For $r\ge m\ge n$, both iterated scalar-association maps multiply the same three coefficient factors, and the input $\alpha^C$ satisfies its cocycle. This proves the output cocycle and normalization, with higher compatibilities supplied by step 1. The coefficient unit system is normalized by the action isomorphism $B_{W,m}\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}\cong B_{W,n}$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); Tag 07A4 and its total-complex coefficient comparisons

proof.text:
For a normalized system $A$, [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] gives the specified coherent counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. By [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], $\mathcal R_W$ is a functor on the derived category, left adjoint to $\mathcal L_W$ as functors between $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_W))$ and the derived system category, and the counit $e$ of this adjunction is a natural transformation $\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W\Rightarrow1$ of derived system maps whose level $n$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of the total-limit projection; this is the canonical counit comparison of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], which is invertible on normalized $A$. Concretely, for $u:A\to A'$ the limit projections satisfy $p'_n\mathcal L(u)=u_np_n$, and naturality of the adjunction counit gives
$$e_{A'}\,\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W(u)=u\,e_A$$
as an equation of system maps in the derived system category, not inferred from evaluations. The simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] retain the coefficient-extension adjunctions used levelwise. We shall use this naturality equation whenever an output of an expression is substituted into another expression.

source.place: Coherent counits of lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity; the derived adjunction R_W -| L_W and its natural counit of lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus

proof.text:
By [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], the defining quotient models give
$$\widehat T_W(K,H)=\mathcal L_W T_W(\mathcal R_WK,\mathcal R_WH),\qquad \widehat F_f(K)=\mathcal L_X F_f(\mathcal R_YK).$$
Here the right sides mean the simultaneous section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], followed by restriction and the total derived-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. They use precisely the actual quotient maps of the definitions. The definitions compute the limit by the complex $\mathsf C=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ on termwise products, whereas $\mathcal L$ is the total derived limit of strict towers. Countable products of module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] supplies the natural isomorphism $\rho:\mathsf C\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim$ on $D(\operatorname{Tow})$, compatible with the projections; we identify the two models by $\rho$. The comparison with the chosen quotient representatives, and its naturality in the inputs, are the resolution-independent functor comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Thus these are functor identifications, not choices of isomorphisms separately at each index.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); defining quotient-limit models; Roos-complex/total-limit comparison of lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison

proof.text:
Substitute $K=\mathcal L_WA$, $H=\mathcal L_WN$ into step 5 and apply the functor $\mathcal L_W$ to the system isomorphism $T_W(e_A,e_N)$. This gives
$$\beta_T:\widehat T_W(\mathcal L_WA,\mathcal L_WN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_W T_W(A,N).$$
Likewise applying $\mathcal L_X$ to $F_f(e_C)$ gives $\beta_F:\widehat F_f(\mathcal L_YC)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_XF_f(C)$. Functors preserve inverses: the inverse system maps are $T_W(e_A^{-1},e_N^{-1})$ and $F_f(e_C^{-1})$. Hence these are exactly the asserted images of the coherent counits, with their naturality from step 4.

source.place: Formal application of the functors and counits in steps 4-5

proof.text:
Define the comparison for a finite expression by structural induction. Write $S_E$ for its value in systems, $K_E$ for its value in completed operations, and $\beta_E:K_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L S_E$ for the claim. For an input system $A$ take $\beta_E=1_{\mathcal LA}$, and for a coefficient unit system $U$ take $\beta_E=1_{\mathcal LU}$. If $E=T(E_1,E_2)$, set
$$\beta_E=\beta_T(S_{E_1},S_{E_2})\circ\widehat T(\beta_{E_1},\beta_{E_2});$$
if $E=F_f(E_1)$, set $\beta_E=\beta_F(S_{E_1})\circ\widehat F_f(\beta_{E_1})$. Steps 2-3 show that every $S_E$ is normalized. The induction is on the number of operation symbols, so every cited child is smaller and these rules cover all well-typed expressions. Every factor is an isomorphism, proving the comparison assertion.

source.place: Finite expression induction using steps 2-3 and 6

proof.text:
For each expression from step 7 define its coherent reduction comparison by
$$\gamma_E=e_{S_E}\circ\mathcal R(\beta_E):\mathcal R K_E\xrightarrow{\sim}S_E.$$
This is an isomorphism of whole systems, since $S_E$ is normalized and [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] supplies a coherent counit. In particular for $m\ge n$ its components satisfy $\tau^{S_E}_{m,n}(\gamma_E)_m=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}((\gamma_E)_n)\tau^{\mathcal RK_E}_{m,n}$, with the coefficient actions implicit. Thus the identification includes every actual quotient transition. No assertion of faithfulness of finite reduction, and no interchange of tensor with an inverse limit, is being used.

source.place: Coherent reduction counit of lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity, applied to the normalized expression of step 7

proof.text: For the finite system reassociator $a:T(T(A,N),H)\to T(A,T(N,H))$, the total-complex formula is $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$; the action unitors are $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$, $x\otimes b\mapsto bx$; symmetry is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in degrees $p,q$. The representative of [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] computes the iterated derived tensors. Apply the natural tensor comparison and its associativity, signed-symmetry and unit clauses in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] to coefficient extension along $B_{W,m}\to B_{W,n}$. They give compatibility of these formulas with scalar extension; its $\varepsilon$ and $\tau$ equations specify the canonical extension transitions. For arbitrary normalized inputs, factor each actual transition through scalar extension and its adjoint $\alpha$, as in steps 2-3. The structural maps are natural in those adjoints: both reassociation routes send $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to the same tensor of their three images; the unit and signed maps have the same check. Composing the scalar-extension square with these naturality squares proves compatibility with the actual input transitions. The coefficient factors have degree zero, so the sign stays $(-1)^{pq}$. The simultaneous constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] retain these maps and compatibilities as coherent system maps. This uses the cited lemma's restricted tower clause only for canonical extension transitions, and naturality for the additional $\alpha$ maps.

source.place: Tag 07A2, total-complex reassociation; Tag 07A4 and Tag 03EL (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback), canonical cochain maps

proof.text:
Let $E_L,E_R$ be the two expressions at either end of one of the tensor system maps $a$ of step 9. The induced map on completed expressions is
$$\beta_{E_R}^{-1}\,\mathcal L(a)\,\beta_{E_L}.$$
It is the canonical completed associator, unitor or signed symmetry: on the quotient models of step 5, inserting the counits as in step 6 yields exactly the respective total-complex formula of step 9. Moving an inserted counit past that formula is justified by its naturality, and replacing a reduction of a limit by the original system is exactly the equation in step 4. Thus under $\beta$ this structural map is $\mathcal L(a)$. Its coherent reduction is the same $a$: the equation $e_{S_{E_R}}\mathcal R\mathcal L(a)=a e_{S_{E_L}}$ gives
$$\gamma_{E_R}\,\mathcal R(\beta_{E_R}^{-1}\mathcal L(a)\beta_{E_L})=a\,\gamma_{E_L}.$$
This proves the specified identification of arrows and their transitions, as well as the identification of vertices.

source.place: Naturality of the explicit maps of step 9 and the counits of step 4; cancellation using the comparisons of steps 7-8

proof.text: For composable scheme maps $Z\xrightarrow{h}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, take $a:F_{f\circ h}(C)\to F_hF_f(C)$. By [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition], its finite module evaluations are the comparisons of left adjoints to the canonical direct-image composition identification. Each coefficient ring is finite and commutative, so [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] makes these pullbacks exact and hence computes their derived versions termwise. On the representatives of step 1, [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] specifies the same adjunction-normalized comparison via scalar association. Its compatibility with changing coefficients is checked on that formula: collapsing the two pullbacks multiplies the two scalar factors, and reducing coefficients before or after collapse agrees because each quotient map preserves multiplication. Inserting $1$ gives the inverse comparison and the same equality. For the actual transition of $C$, first use this scalar-extension square and then naturality of $a$ for $\alpha^C_{m,n}$, using the factorization in step 3. This proves the required transition square without applying the canonical-transition tower clause to an arbitrary normalized input. The section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserve these specified composition and adjunction constructions, giving a coherent system map. Apply the conjugation formula of step 10 to $a$; its counit naturality equation identifies the limit with the completed composition comparison and the coherent reduction with the finite adjunction-normalized map.

Finally induct on expression size for naturality and substitution. At a leaf naturality is the identity square. At a tensor vertex the square is the composite of the two child squares with naturality of $T(e,e)$ from step 4; at a pullback vertex it is the child square followed by naturality of $F(e)$. Applying the functor $\mathcal L$ preserves these squares. For substitution of expressions $H_i$ into the input slots of $E$, compare the flattened recursion of step 7 with first applying $\beta_{H_i}$ and then the recursion for $E$. At each vertex the only extra replacement is $\mathcal R\mathcal L S_{H_i}\xrightarrow{e_{S_{H_i}}}S_{H_i}$. Moving that replacement past a child comparison uses $e_{S'}\mathcal R\mathcal L(u)=u e_S$ from step 4. After that move the two composites are identical by functoriality and associativity of composition. The leaf case is identity, and tensor and pullback are all constructors, so the induction proves compatibility for every finite substitution. It also applies to the maps in steps 9-11, which were natural system maps before the limit.

source.place: Formal induction on finite syntax; explicit counit naturality equation of step 4

Refreshed all three affected verbatim quotations; all other cited quotations remain current.
